note_on_method: Each venue page rests on two City of Cape Coral pages: the Park Sports/Games page that counts the courts and prices them, and the park's own page that gives the address and the amenities. The US Census address geocoder and OpenStreetMap supply the county and the postcode. Where the City is silent, these pages record the silence.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts with lights in a 6.4-acre neighbourhood park in south-west Cape Coral, free and open until 9:00 p.m. daily.

The City writes this venue as a configuration rather than an inventory: "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts". One pair of tennis slabs, set up either way. The park's own page describes the same ground from the tennis end, as "Two (lighted) Tennis Courts that include court lines for Pickleball".

The City calls the park "nestled in a beautiful single family area". It has a circular three-tenths-of-a-mile paved walking path around the perimeter, picnic pavilions with BBQ grills, a playground for ages 2 to 12, and restrooms.
slots.getting_there:
1718 SW 52 Terrace, Cape Coral, FL 33914, in Lee County.

The street type matters here. The US Census geocoder answers this address with "1718 SW 52ND ST": right county, right postcode, wrong street. Cape Coral's grid carries a Street, a Terrace, a Lane and a Court at the same number, and SW 52nd Terrace and SW 52nd Street are about seventy-seven metres apart. OpenStreetMap finds the address as the City writes it, and that is what is published here.

The City publishes nothing about parking. There are restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts if the slabs are set up for pickleball, two tennis courts if they are not. The City publishes the configuration as an either/or rather than a schedule, so there is no way to know before you arrive.

Play is free: the City states that its park tennis and pickleball courts are "available for public use at no charge". The courts are lit and stay open until 9:00 p.m. every day.

The City says nothing about the surface, nothing about parking, and nothing about when the courts are busy. It also never describes these courts as indoor or outdoor, so this site does not either, though a park with a perimeter walking path and BBQ grills leaves little doubt.

faqs.a: Four pickleball courts, on two convertible tennis slabs. The City writes it as "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts with lights".

faqs.q: Why does a map search show a different street?
faqs.a: The City's address is 1718 SW 52 Terrace. The Census geocoder answers that with SW 52nd Street, a different street about seventy-seven metres away. This site publishes the Terrace, as the City writes it.

slots.description:
Two dedicated pickleball courts, not tennis courts wearing a second set of lines, in the oldest neighbourhood park in Cape Coral.

This is the one venue in the city the City counts twice. Its Park Sports/Games page states two dedicated pickleball courts and no lights, and the park's own page lists "Two Pickleball Courts" among its amenities, independently. Every other Cape Coral park page describes its courts without numbering them.

That stated absence of lights matters beyond this park. An operator willing to write a negative down when it is true is an operator whose silences, like the one at Sands Park, are real silences.

The park is 3.7 acres and, in the City's words, "was the first neighborhood park in Cape Coral". It has picnic pavilions with BBQ grills, a playground for ages 2 to 12 and restrooms.
slots.getting_there:
1044 NE 4 Street, Cape Coral, FL 33909, in the north-east of the city.

The US Census address geocoder matched the address at house-number level and placed it in the incorporated place Cape Coral, Lee County. This is the one published Cape Coral venue where the Census answer needed no second opinion, because the City's street type and the Census's agree.

The City publishes nothing about parking here. There are restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Two courts, dedicated to pickleball, free, and finishing at sunset.

The sunset is stated rather than inferred. The City marks this venue as having no lights, and its general rule is that park courts are open "from sunrise to sunset (or later for locations with lighting)". Cape Coral's three lit venues stay open to 9 p.m. This one does not.

With only two courts and no lights, this is a place for a game rather than a rotation. The City publishes no surface, no parking information and nothing about when it is busy. What it does give you is certainty on two questions: what the courts are, and what they cost.

faqs.a: No, and that is stated rather than assumed: the City marks this venue as having no lights. The courts close at sunset.
Yes. The City calls them dedicated, which distinguishes them from the three Cape Coral venues where tennis slabs convert into pickleball courts.

slots.description:
Six pickleball courts, the largest published pickleball venue in Cape Coral, on an 18.7-acre athletic park in the north-west of the city.

The six is the City's own arithmetic. Its sports page gives "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts" with lights, open until 9:00 p.m. daily, and then adds "and two (2) warm-up pickleball courts". Four on the convertible tennis slabs, plus two warm-up courts counted separately.

One consequence belongs on the page rather than in a footnote. The City's "with lights" attaches to the four, not to the two. Whether the warm-up courts are lit is not something it says.

The park around them is the busiest site in published Cape Coral: a three-acre lake, four lighted soccer fields, lighted basketball courts, three picnic pavilions with BBQ grills, a playground for ages 4 to 17, restrooms and walking paths.
slots.getting_there:
2817 SW 3 Lane, Cape Coral, FL 33991, in Lee County.

As at Camelot Park, the street type matters. The Census geocoder answers this address with "2817 SW 3RD ST", and SW 3rd Lane is a different street. OpenStreetMap finds the Lane as the City writes it, and that is the resolution published here.

The City publishes nothing about parking, which is a more noticeable gap at an eighteen-acre park with four soccer fields than at the smaller sites. There are restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Six courts is enough for a rotation, which makes this the one Cape Coral venue where turning up alone is a reasonable plan. Play is free and the main four courts are lit until 9:00 p.m. daily.

This is an athletic park: four lighted soccer fields and lighted basketball courts share the site, and the City notes that picnic pavilions at athletic parks are first-come, first-served. On an evening when the fields are in use, the park will be busy even if the courts are not.

Four of the six courts are tennis slabs configured for pickleball rather than dedicated courts, so what you find depends on the setup. The City publishes no surface, no parking and no information about peak times.

faqs.a: Six. Four on the convertible tennis slabs, plus two warm-up pickleball courts the City counts separately on the same line.
The City's "with lights" applies to the four courts on the tennis slabs. It says nothing either way about the two warm-up courts.

slots.description:
Four pickleball courts with lights in a seven-acre park arranged around a one-acre lake, free and open until 9:00 p.m. daily.

The City writes this venue exactly as it writes Camelot: "Two (2) tennis courts -OR- Four (4) pickleball courts". Two tennis slabs configured as four pickleball courts. The park's own page gives the tennis-side description, "Two (lighted) Tennis Courts that include court lines for Pickleball", so both City records describe the same ground and the pickleball number comes from the sports page.

The City calls the park "beautifully landscaped", and the amenity list bears that out: a one-acre lake, two picnic pavilions with BBQ grills, a playground for ages 2 to 12, restrooms and walking paths.
slots.getting_there:
3444 Ceitus Parkway, Cape Coral, FL 33991.

This address resolves through OpenStreetMap rather than the US Census address file, and for a different reason from the other Cape Coral venues: the Census simply holds no record of Ceitus Parkway. OpenStreetMap matches it at house-number level, in Lee County, in the incorporated place Cape Coral.

The City publishes nothing about parking. There are restrooms.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four courts when the slabs are set up for pickleball, lit until 9:00 p.m., free.

Four courts is a workable number without being a complex. Because they are lit and cost nothing, the evening is the window most people will use, though that is a reading of the published hours rather than a stated fact.

What the City does not say applies here as everywhere in this city: no surface, no parking, no busy periods, and no statement that these courts are indoor or outdoor. The one thing worth planning around is the configuration. Four pickleball courts exist when the slabs are set up for pickleball, and two tennis courts exist when they are not.

faqs.a: Yes, and the courts stay open until 9:00 p.m. daily.

faqs.q: Why does this address resolve differently?
faqs.a: The US Census address file holds no record of Ceitus Parkway, so this venue is resolved by OpenStreetMap, which matches it at house-number level.

slots.description:
Four dedicated pickleball courts, pickleball courts rather than tennis courts lending themselves to the game, in a park with an unusually varied set of neighbours.

The City's line is short and unambiguous: "Four (4) dedicated pickleball courts". Together with Giuffrida Park's two, these are the only dedicated pickleball courts published in Cape Coral. Every other published court in the city sits on a convertible tennis slab or is a warm-up court.

The park itself, in the City's description, "offers walking paths, a putting green, a playground, a burrowing owl habitat area, a butterfly plant garden, and sports courts for basketball, tennis, pickleball, bocce ball, and cornhole".
slots.getting_there:
2718 SW 43rd Terrace, Cape Coral, FL 33914, in south-west Cape Coral.

The street type matters here as it does across this city. The Census geocoder answers with "2718 SW 43RD ST", a different street, and OpenStreetMap finds the Terrace exactly as the City writes it. That is the resolution published here, in Lee County, in the incorporated place Cape Coral.

The City publishes nothing about parking at this park, and unlike the other four published venues its amenity list does not mention restrooms either. That absence is recorded as unknown rather than as a no.
slots.what_to_expect:
Four dedicated courts, free, and the one open question in Cape Coral's otherwise complete lighting record.

The City marks lights at Camelot, Jim Jeffers and Joe Stonis, and marks their absence at Giuffrida. About Sands Park it says nothing at all. Because this is an operator that writes the negative down when it applies, that silence is treated as a genuine gap. Lighting here is recorded as unverified, and the safe plan is to be off the court by sunset until the City says otherwise.

Everything else is settled. The courts are dedicated, there are four of them, and they cost nothing. The City publishes no surface and no information about busy periods, and it never calls these courts indoor or outdoor.

faqs.a: Not stated. The City marks lighting at other Cape Coral venues and marks its absence at Giuffrida Park, and about Sands it says nothing either way, so this site records it as unverified.
The City's amenity list for this park does not mention them, and does mention them at the other four published venues. That is recorded as unknown rather than as a no.
